newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - July 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - July 10.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government has raised $300 million from the international market through the sale of a special bond.
- The United Arab Emirates has agreed to give Pakistan $300 million three-year medium term soft loan.
- Pakistan and India will discuss next month a proposal to set up joint working groups as a follow-up to the second round of foreign secretary level talks.
- The United Nation special envoy on Afghanistan Norbert Holl leaves for Mazar-e-Sharif on Thursday for talks with the northern alliance leaders for a ceasefire with Taleban.

- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan would not allow the government to borrow more than 55 billion rupees from the banking system in the current fiscal 1997/98 (July-June) to narrow down the budget deficit.

- Commercial banks may reduce interest rates by one percent in the last quarter of 1997, if not earlier, in pursuance of the government policy to slash the mark-up rates by two percent by the end of the fiscal 1997/98.
- The European Union is likely to initiate anti-dumping proceedings against unbleached cotton fabrics from Pakistan that will hamper local exports worth $100 million to the Union.

- A World Bank team will arrive in Karachi by the end of month to discuss financial assistance to the state-run Karachi Port Trust including release of $187 million for modernisation of the Karachi Port that will cost $350 million.

- History was created at the Karachi Stock Exchange when volume touched an all time high level of 159 million shares while the index raced up to the 16 month high mark of 1,778.51 on bulk buying from British and U.S. investors.
- A record production of local edible oils has been estimated in the current year that would reduce the volume of Pakistani imports of plam and soya oils from abroad.
